items.teaser: Most families think they know what UC readers are looking for — GPA, test scores, a long activities list. They're usually wrong, and it's costing strong students real opportunities. Former UC Berkeley admissions reader Brennan reveals what actually happens when a file gets opened, and how to build a UC application that tells one clear, unmistakable story.

children.text: Most families think they know what UC readers are looking for — GPA, test scores, a long activities list. They're usually wrong and it's costing strong students real opportunities. Join Brennan, a former UC Berkeley admissions reader, for Real Strategies to Get Into UCs, a live session that goes beyond the UC website and into what actually happens when a file gets opened. You'll learn why the same GPA can read completely differently at two different campuses, why longer activity lists often work against students, and how to build a UC application that tells one clear, unmistakable story.
The UC GPA your student thinks they have is often not the one admissions readers calculate — and that gap changes which campuses are realistic.
UC doesn't reward busy. Two activities with real impact consistently outperform ten shallow ones — you'll learn exactly what "impact" means to a reader.
With no interviews and no letters of rec, the four PIQs carry the entire weight of who your student is. Most students waste them repeating the resume.

children.text: Getting into Texas' most competitive colleges takes more than good grades — it takes a strategic, well-rounded application that speaks directly to what each school values. In this webinar, a college admissions expert will break down what top Texas universities like UT Austin, Texas A&M, and Rice University are really looking for in their applicants. Learn how to position your academics, extracurriculars, and essays to align with each school's unique admissions criteria and stand out in a highly competitive applicant pool. Walk away with a clear, actionable plan to build a compelling application that maximizes your chances of getting into your top Texas college.
UT Austin, Texas A&M, Rice, and SMU read applications nothing alike. Learn which rules actually apply to your student's target schools.
Top 5% gets your student into UT Austin — it guarantees nothing about the major they named. Competitive programs run their own, much tighter review.
SMU applicants who engage early and apply ED can unlock $20K–$40K a year in merit aid — most families never do the work to earn it.

items.title: 10 Things Top Colleges Want to See in Your Student
items.teaser: Every year, families guess at what colleges want — and end up polishing the wrong things. Former Johns Hopkins admissions officer Ford, who reviewed over 8,000 applications, breaks down the 10 qualities top colleges actually prioritize in 2026, and where most students focus their energy in the wrong place. Whether your student is just starting out or deep into applications, this session shows you what really moves the needle.

meta.description: Every year, families guess at what colleges want and end up polishing the wrong things. Join this webinar to learn about what colleges look for.

children.text: Every year, thousands of applications cross an admissions officer's desk, and most families are optimizing for the wrong signals. Join Ford, a former Assistant Director of Admissions at Johns Hopkins University, for a data-driven look inside what admissions officers are actually evaluating in the 2026 cycle. You'll learn the 10 key qualities colleges weigh across academics, extracurriculars, essays, and recommendations, how each one shows up (or fails to show up) in a real application, and where families commonly misjudge what matters. Whether your student is early in the process or already building their list, this session will help you focus on the traits that count and build them intentionally over time. Come with questions — Ford has read the applications that got in, and the ones that didn't.

Admissions officers aren't scoring a checklist — they're reading for specific signals across academics, activities, essays, and recommendations. Ford breaks down exactly what those signals look like in a real file.
Many students spend their energy polishing what colleges barely notice, while missing what actually drives decisions. Learn which signals get overlooked and why.
Building It Over Time, Not Overnight:
These qualities aren't manufactured senior year — they're built intentionally, starting now. Get a practical framework for developing them before it's too late to show.
